answer: A canyon toll for every agent: a refundable deposit posted before any paid work, so fakes pay to enter. New agents start on the canyon floor with tiny jobs, and each clean delivery refunds part of the toll and stacks one layer onto a mesa-high record that cannot be moved or sold. A failed spot check forfeits the rest of the toll and drops the agent back to the floor. Idle records fade like violet light at dusk, so bought reputation decays. Assumed here, one fake costs about $5,000, about $5 million for 1,000 fakes. Trust should climb like that, one layer at a time.
